newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Monday after a slightly softer start and dealers said buyers were mainly private investors who were speculating on the publication of strong annual company results this week.

Hagemeyer, ABN AMRO and DSM rose ahead of their results announcements. "DSM is expected to show a drop in net profits of about 33 percent in 1996, that is better than earlier expected," said one dealer. The stock rose 5.90 guilders to 185.00.
DSM said in January its preliminary net over 1996 would be at least 700 million guilders.
The AEX share index ended 4.59 points higher at 733.51.
"Volumes were low today as market players were somewhat nervous," said one dealer.
Earlier today some Dutch chartists warned of a short-term correction this week, but added that the outlook for the longer run remained positive.
The Dutch share index ignored the weaker bond market and the lower dollar though, and rose even further in late afternoon after the Dow Jones started climbing in its opening half hour.
Hagemeyer jumped 7.40 guilders to close at a new high of 157.00 guilders ahead of Wednesday's 1996 results.
ABN AMRO bank closed at another high, up 4.10 guilders at 140.50 ahead of its 1996 results announcement on Thursday.
"The expectations are high for ABN AMRO and the continuing rumours on a share split also boosted business," said one dealer.
Analysts forecast last week that ABN AMRO would report a 26 percent leap in annual net profit to 3.29 billion guilders.
Steel and aluminium group Hoogovens rose 5.00 guilders to 83.50 as result of a buy-recommendation from broker Goldman Sachs.
Paper maker KNP BT performed well with a rise of 1.30 guilders to 43.10.
Food group Nutricia rose nearly three percent to 287.30 guilders, climbing near to its previous high of 289.00 guilders on February 18.
CSM, which was transferred from the AEX index into the Midcap-index today, gained 2.80 guilders to 113.40.
